subject: Greenline - private endpoint allowlist & firewall governance
messages:
From: Greenline SecOps <secops@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme IT Integrations <itops@acme-it.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Private endpoint: allowlist and firewall requirements

Hi Jordan —

We're preparing our firewall change window for the Greenline pilot and need a definitive allowlist + outbound policy from Redwood to give to our network team and Acme (cc'd). Specifically we need:
- A minimal set of IPs/CIDRs and ports that must be permitted for the private (VPC/on‑prem) runtime to talk to Redwood control plane and telemetry.
- Any required FQDNs/DNS entries (we prefer allowing FQDNs if possible).
- Expected outbound ports (we'd like to limit to 443 only if you support it).
- A short description of what happens if our network only permits egress via a corporate proxy (transparent proxy or explicit proxy).
- Proof artifacts for procurement/SOC2: an IP evidence CSV or manifest we can keep in our change ticket.

Constraints:
- No permanent inbound holes — everything must be outbound only.
- We rotate NAT addresses nightly via our cloud automation and can provide a small ephemeral range for the pilot, but we need Redwood to accept an allowlist model (you provide stable control plane IPs or endpoints).

Can you send a short checklist + sample firewall rules? We're targeting the change on Monday 2026‑09‑20.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
SecOps Manager, Greenline Health

Attachments: Greenline_SOW_v3.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Greenline SecOps <secops@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Acme IT Integrations <itops@acme-it.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint: allowlist and firewall requirements

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise allowlist + options matrix you can drop into your change ticket and hand to Acme. I've attached a CSV with the control plane/egress IPs we certify for the next 90 days (redwood-ip-evidence-20260913.csv) and a short PDF summary (redwood_onprem_allowlist_v1.pdf).

Minimal allowlist (recommended)
- Destination IPs: 34.213.128.0/23, 52.12.64.0/22, 18.197.0.0/20 (these are our control plane egress points; attach csv for full list)
- Ports: 443 (outbound TLS).
- Protocols: HTTPS (TLS1.2+); OCSP/CRL via standard ports permitted by TLS.
- DNS: Allow outbound resolution to *.redwood-inference.com and our cert validation endpoints (ocsp.redwood-inference.com). If you prefer FQDNs only, make sure your proxy preserves SNI and hostname in CONNECT (not all proxies do).

Telemetry & Ops endpoints (optional for stricter customers)
- telemetry-collector.redwood-inference.com (443) — used for metrics/logs
- opt-in: metrics can be disabled in Private deployment if you require air‑gap-like behavior; let us know.

Proxy / Corporate NAT guidance
- If you have an explicit outbound proxy (HTTP CONNECT), we require TLS passthrough to preserve certificate validation (we cannot operate if the proxy performs active TLS MITM unless you provide a TLS bridging certificate and accept the security implications).
- If egress is forced through a corporate NAT, we support two modes: 1) You permit the static control plane CIDRs above, or 2) You provide an SNAT pool and we will accept ephemeral CIDR assertions via an automated webhook for the pilot window. Mode 2 requires mutual auth and is suitable if you rotate nightly.

Failover / fallback behavior
- If an outbound connection to the control plane is blocked, the runtime will keep local inference serving (no control-plane upgrades) but will queue telemetry and rollout events for later delivery. Critical control plane operations (new model downloads, rollouts that require coordination) will fail with clear error states — we will provide a fallback playbook.

Next steps & action items
- Jordan: provide final signed CSV + PDF (attached).
- Greenline/Acme: confirm which mode you prefer (static CIDR vs SNAT assertion webhook) and whether the pilot permits outbound port 443.
- Laura: can you add a short runbook snippet for the SNAT assertion webhook?

I'll follow up with a short runbook and the HubSpot ticket link.

—Jordan
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_onprem_allowlist_v1.pdf, redwood-ip-evidence-20260913.csv
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Greenline SecOps <secops@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Acme IT Integrations <itops@acme-it.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint: allowlist and firewall requirements

Thanks — adding a few technical clarifications from an ops/runbook perspective.

1) TLS and DNS considerations- We require SNI-preserving CONNECT behavior when a proxy is present. If the proxy terminates TLS, please provide the signing cert or use an explicit allowlist + mutual TLS for the outbound channel.

2) DNS allowlisting vs IP allowlisting- FQDN rules are easier operationally but fail when endpoints move under our load balancers. If you rely only on FQDNs, include a small IP buffer in the firewall (our CSV includes the current set) and a process to revalidate IPs weekly.

3) SNAT assertion webhook (recommended for rotating NATs)
- We will accept a signed JSON assertion from your network automation to https://hooks.redwood-inference.com/egress-assertions- Payload: list of current SNAT IPs, valid_from, valid_until, signed with your key.- Acceptance: Redwood will validate signature + validity window and accept the SNATs for up to 24 hours.
- If you cannot run the webhook, use option (static CIDR) for the pilot.

4) Evidence for procurement / SOC2- The attached CSV is timestamped and signed by our infra team. For SOC2, we can provide an Signed IP Manifest and a short note describing change control (if procurement requires an attestation doc, tell me the contact and I'll route it through security).

Runbook excerpt attached: egress-handshake-runbook.md

Laura 
Principal Engineer, Runtime & Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: egress-handshake-runbook.md

Jordan / Laura — thanks for the clear docs. Greenline's change window is confirmed for 2026‑09‑20 02:00–04:00 UTC. A few notes from the integrator side:
- Greenline will prefer the SNAT assertion webhook approach because they rotate NATs nightly. We'll implement the webhook and mutual auth; Acme will present the signed payloads during a dry run next Thursday.
- Can Redwood confirm the webhook auth mechanism (we prefer mTLS + an HMAC header on the payload).
- Procurement asked for one more artifact: a short explanation of fallback semantics when control plane is unreachable (we need this for our CAB).

Can you send the webhook spec and a one-paragraph fallback statement we can paste into the CAB packet?

—Daniel Ortega
Lead Integration Engineer, Acme IT
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Greenline SecOps <secops@greenlinehealth.com>, Acme IT Integrations <itops@acme-it.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private endpoint: allowlist and firewall requirements

Daniel / Maya — great, thanks. Quick deliverables we've attached/linked and the two‑paragraph fallback text below for your CAB:
- Webhook auth: we support mTLS for the hook endpoint plus an HMAC-SHA256 X-Redwood-Signature header. We'll share a test cert and endpoint in the HubSpot ticket.
- Fallback statement (copy/paste):
  If Redwood's control plane becomes unreachable, the on‑prem runtime will continue serving inference from cached models for active sessions. Non‑critical telemetry and analytics will queue locally and be delivered when connectivity is restored. Administrative operations that require control plane coordination (new model activations, global rollouts, or revocations) will not be performed during the outage — these actions will return clear error codes and must be retried after connectivity is restored. For high‑assurance use cases, schedule a maintenance window for rollout operations or use a staged canary with a controlled failover.

Action items:
- Acme: implement webhook + dry run (test next Thu).
- Greenline: confirm pilot scope (models allowed to serve from cache) and provide contact for procurement attestation.
- Jordan: attach HubSpot deal link and open a brief DocuSign for the commercial pilot addendum.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/GL-8421
DocuSign: https://docusign.redwood.com/link/GL-8421-PilotAddendum

I'll check back after the dry run and provide the signed IP manifest for procurement.

—Jordan

Redwood Inference
